Thanks, Olga — quick pass below. I've focused on the product-facing acceptance criteria. I kept items short so AlphaStream can read the checklist in one pass.

1) Baseline prompts and test set
- We require a canonical prompt set (50 seed prompts) that represents the top-40% of their real traffic (examples supplied).

2) Quality acceptance thresholds (A vs B)
- Automatic metrics: perplexity delta < 2% AND token-level F1 on labeled subset >= 0.75.
- Human eval (5 raters, 30 responses per variant): mean usefulness score delta >= +0.15 to qualify as a win.

3) Safety & hallucination gate
- Hallucination incidents (as defined in doc) must be <= 0.5% on the labeled set for both variants. Any model crossing 1.0% triggers immediate pause.

4) Latency guard
- P95 generation latency must not exceed baseline + 120ms for critical flows.

5) Rollout plan
- Canary 5% for 48h -> 20% for 72h -> 100% if no safety/quality triggers.

Notes: I left open the exact human-eval rubric — we should link to QA-9482 for the rubric details.

Marissa
Product Manager, Model Quality

Adding telemetry constraints. High level: we need the minimal surface that procurement + security expect and what product needs to detect regressions.

Telemetry (minimum):
- Per-request: model_id, variant_tag, request_id, client_id, prompt_hash, latency_ms (server), p95_stream_ms, token_count
- Quality signals: automated hallucination flag, human_eval_id (when sampled), safety_flag_cats
- Aggregates: hourly per-variant error rate, hallucination rate (labeled), average usefulness score (human-eval rollups)

Retention & access:
- Raw per-request logs: 30 days (hosted) / configurable for Dedicated (default 90d if requested)
- Aggregates: 13 months
- We will expose a dashboard link and provide a CSV dump on request each week during the trial.

Alerting (suggestion):
- Immediate (pager): hallucination rate > 1.0% for 15m window OR error rate > 3%
- Rollback candidate: sudden drop in human-eval mean usefulness by > 0.20 vs baseline

Cost note: enabling per-request retention at 90d on Hosted increases S3 and query costs; for AlphaStream we'll include an optional Dedicated estimate in the SOW.

Ben
Director, Observability

Couple of practical engineering constraints to call out so product and ops can set realistic expectations:

1) Model variants:
- We should ensure both A and B run on the same quantization profile for the pilot. If AlphaStream asks to compare a 4-bit quantized variant vs a 16-bit, the metric noise will be high; we'll flag that as "not suitable for A/B" in the checklist.

2) KV cache priming:
- Any prefix caching differences will bias latencies. For the canary, we'll prime caches uniformly and document the priming steps in the checklist.

3) Fallbacks & routing:
- Our smart routing may fallback to a lower-cost variant under tight capacity. For a controlled A/B, we need a pinning rule to prevent cross-variant fallback. That will require a short policy change in routing (estimate: 2 engineer-days).

4) E2E reproducibility:
- Seed logging and deterministic dispatch are enabled only in Dedicated today. On Hosted, we'll approximate but will note variance in results.

I'll mark the checklist fields that are 'engineering blockers' vs 'product OK'.

Karthik
Sr. Eng Manager, Serving Runtime
